requirements.text: Design and implement a cloud-native claims intake platform supporting minimum 50,000 claims/day
Integrate with existing Guidewire ClaimCenter via published APIs
AI-assisted document classification for claims correspondence, minimum 95% accuracy
Encryption of data at rest and in transit (AES-256 / TLS 1.2+)
US-hosted solution compliant with SOC 2 Type II
Real-time fraud-detection scoring on all incoming claims (sub-second latency preferred)
24x7 production support with 15-minute Severity 1 response SLA
Migrate 7 years (~40 TB) of historical claims data with full audit traceability
Complete implementation within 12 months of contract award
Unlimited liability coverage for data breaches from Vendor negligence
All IP developed under the engagement transfers to Acme
Three references from insurance-industry clients of similar size
Maintain adequate staffing as deemed appropriate by Acme

ambiguities: Clause 3.7: 'sub-second latency preferred' - unclear whether sub-second is mandatory or desirable
Clause 4.6: 'adequate staffing as deemed appropriate by Acme' is undefined and unilaterally determined by the client
risky_terms: Clause 4.2: unlimited liability for data breaches - exceeds standard liability caps
Clause 4.3: full IP transfer would include pre-existing accelerators unless carved out
Clause 3.9: 15-minute Sev-1 SLA is stricter than standard 30-minute commitment

mappings.evidence: CAP-01 platform practice has delivered 120k transactions/day, above the 50k requirement.
CAP-02: certified Guidewire partner with 6 ClaimCenter API integrations.
CAP-03 document AI accelerator achieved 96-98% accuracy on insurance correspondence.
CAP-07: four insurance claimant portals delivered, React Native mobile-first.
CAP-04 standard patterns cover AES-256 and TLS 1.3.
CAP-04: SOC 2 Type II attested; US-only hosting available.
CAP-06 standard Sev-1 SLA is 30 minutes; 15-minute SLA only at premium tier - price accordingly.
CAP-05 migration factory is audit-traceable but largest prior migration was 25 TB vs. 40 TB required.
CAP-01 supports phased delivery; 12-month full scope is aggressive given 40 TB migration - propose phased plan.
CAP-06 managed-services practice includes standard knowledge-transfer methodology.
CAP-01/CAP-07: multiple insurance references available (2 carriers, 4 portal clients).
Staffing commitments supported, but clause as written is open-ended - needs clarification.

clarification_questions: Clause 3.7: Is sub-second fraud-scoring latency mandatory, or is near-real-time (<5s) acceptable?
Clause 4.2: Will Acme accept a liability cap (e.g., 2x annual fees) with cyber-insurance backing instead of unlimited liability?
Clause 4.3: Can pre-existing vendor IP and accelerators be excluded from IP transfer, with Acme receiving a perpetual license?
Clause 4.6: Can 'adequate staffing' be defined via agreed staffing plan and change-control process?
